video_title: Why Yuki Kawamura (河村勇輝) Was One Of My Favorite NBA Teammates EVER

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Yuki Kawamura's high basketball IQ and decision-making in pick-and-roll
quotes.excerpt: Yuki is a smart player and he understands his size and that he's got to be able to get shots off quick.
quotes.quote: Yuki starts to come off this screen, he holds his guy in a hostage position. You keep the guy in jail, your defender in jail, and you make this big man make a decision. Yuki is a smart player and he understands his size and that he's got to be able to get shots off quick. He doesn't have time for these slow one-two steps. Yuki is a smart player and he understands his size and that he's got to be able to get shots off quick.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Yuki Kawamura's ability to exploit defensive mistakes by LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: Yuki recognizes both LeBron's hands are down and he lets it fly.
quotes.quote: As he catches the ball, LeBron's hands are both down. Most teams will teach when you are closing out to a guy that can shoot the ball, you carry an early stick hand. Yuki recognizes both LeBron's hands are down and he lets it fly. Yuki is a very good shooter and he can shoot from a little bit behind the line, so he recognizes a guy closes out with their hands down, you let it fly.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Yuki Kawamura's playmaking and baiting Bam Adebayo into defensive errors
quotes.excerpt: Yuki does a good job of baiting him and selling it but he's going to shoot a layup.
quotes.quote: Bam Adebayo, who is as good of a shot blocker as there is in the league, Yuki is probably not going to try to lay this up over Bam. He acts like he is going to lay it up. Bam jumps to contest the shot and rightfully so, Yuki does a good job of selling it and at the last second, he dumps it off. Yuki is a very, very good passer and Bam is a great shot blocker.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Yuki Kawamura's elite transition playmaking and passing vision
quotes.excerpt: When Yuki is in transition and does something like this, you just know a highlight pass is coming.
quotes.quote: He is obviously as fast as a lot of guards. It is pretty much a three-on-one. He has Gerschon Yabusele on one side, he has Matas Buzelis on the other side. When Yuki is in transition and does something like this, you just know a highlight pass is coming. He throws a wrap-around behind-the-back pass. I don't even know if Matas was expecting it. Matas probably thinks it is going to Yabusele, his hands aren't really ready for the ball and Yuki drops it off to him.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Yuki Kawamura's ability to create open shots through off-ball movement
quotes.excerpt: It is Lenny's responsibility to cut out of here out of the slot because if the ball goes back to
quotes.quote: We teach when a guy pops, the big man that can shoot the ball pops, the other guy in the slot, it is a side of three. It is Lenny's responsibility to cut out of here out of the slot because if the ball goes back to, if Lenny stays there, his man can easily stunt at, which means hedge and pretend like he is going to help to allow the defender to get back to the ball. But because Lenny cuts, it is late. If Yuki hit Lenny, look how open the shot is for Lenny because of Lenny's cut.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Yuki Kawamura's craftiness and ability to find teammates in the paint
quotes.excerpt: He is someone that can very easily get to the paint and make players around him better.
quotes.quote: It looks like a normal drag screen, but Yuki rejects the pick and roll. Starts to get downhill. Very crafty guard as well, for his size, he is someone that can very easily get to the paint and make players around him better. I think that is one of his best skills, his ability to get in the paint and find different and find players and make players around him better. Sharif Cooper, who is the smaller guy of these two Wizards guys, the guy on the elbow here, Championship, is on Pat. As Yuki drives here, attracts attention, Championship helps, Pat cuts, the unsung hero of the play, he draws a defender and it allows Yuki to jump pass wide open to the corner.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Yuki Kawamura's rare ability to win jump balls as a guard
quotes.excerpt: Not many times is Yuki probably going to win a jump ball, but he did on this instance.
quotes.quote: Not many times is Yuki probably going to win a jump ball, but he did on this instance and we were on the bench going nuts when this happened because not many times is Yuki probably going to win a jump ball, but he did on this instance and we all loved it on the bench.
